title: Certificates of Deposit: opening a certificate, the opening deposit and the term dates
content:
## Scope

This policy governs how a certificate of the Certificates of Deposit line is opened, what the opening deposit must be, and how funding fixes the term start date and the maturity date. Its clause on PCB funding accounts applies to every deposit into a certificate, not only the opening deposit. It applies to every tier, each tier supplying its own minimum and maximum opening deposit, its new-money requirement, its accepted funding sources and its term length.

## Policy clauses

1. **Opening.** A certificate opens in applied status at the rate and APY fixed on the opening date, and awaits funding.
2. **Age.** The customer's age in whole years on the opening date, taken from the date of birth on the customer profile, must be at least the tier's minimum age to open.
3. **Opening deposit.** The opening deposit must be a single deposit of at least the tier's minimum opening deposit and at most the tier's maximum principal, arriving by one of the tier's accepted funding sources.
4. **New money.** On a tier that requires new money, an internal transfer from any PCB account is not accepted.
5. **Funding and term dates.** The certificate is funded, and becomes active, on the business day the opening deposit posts. The term start date is that posting date. The maturity date is the term start date moved forward by the tier's term length in calendar months, falling back to the last day of the month when that day does not exist in the maturity month.
6. **Deposits from PCB accounts.** Any deposit into a certificate from a PCB checking or PCB savings account, whether the opening deposit, a grace-period add-on or an in-term add-on, debits that account, and that account must belong to the same customer.

## Basis of decision

- The age is judged from the date of birth recorded on the customer profile, as a system record, before the certificate is opened; it is not taken from the customer's statement.
- The term start date is the posting date of the opening deposit, not the opening date.

## Opening checklist

| Check | Passes when |
|---|---|
| Age on the opening date | Whole years from the recorded date of birth are at least the tier's minimum age |
| Number of deposits | The opening deposit is a single deposit |
| Size of the opening deposit | At least the tier minimum and at most the tier maximum |
| Funding source | One of the tier's accepted sources; no internal PCB transfer where the tier requires new money |
| Internal source account | A PCB checking or savings account of the same customer |

## Illustrative age cases

- A customer reaches the tier's minimum age exactly on the opening date. The age in whole years on that date equals the minimum, so the age check passes.
- A customer reaches the tier's minimum age on the day after the opening date. On the opening date the age in whole years is one below the minimum, so the age check fails.

## Illustrative maturity dates (hypothetical posting dates and term lengths)

| Opening deposit posts on (term start date) | Hypothetical term length | Maturity date |
|---|---|---|
| 15 January 2027 | 6 months | 15 July 2027 |
| 31 August 2026 | 6 months | 28 February 2027 (31 February does not exist) |
| 31 August 2027 | 6 months | 29 February 2028 (the last day of February in a leap year) |
| 31 March 2026 | 12 months | 31 March 2027 |

## Points of judgement

**The certificate was opened on one day and funded two days later. Which date starts the term?**
The posting date of the opening deposit, two days later, is the term start date.

**May the opening deposit be split into two deposits that each fall within the tier's range?**
No. The opening deposit must be a single deposit.
